memory_update.text: CAMT belongs in the HBM advanced-packaging second-layer universe as an inspection/metrology candidate with direct HBM, chiplet, and hybrid-bonding language in 2026 SEC and investor materials.
FORM belongs in the HBM second-layer universe as a probe-card/test candidate; strongest evidence to verify is HBM DRAM customer expansion and HBM4-related probe-card demand.
KLIC belongs in the HBM second-layer universe as a speculative-to-underfollowed bonding-equipment candidate; key survival test is whether first HBM system shipment converts to repeat revenue.
Inspection/metrology, probe cards, and bonding tools appear to be the most evidence-backed US-listed public-market mappings for HBM and advanced-packaging second-layer supplier exposure in this pass.

The useful underfollowed gap is not simply small market cap; it is mismatch between HBM qualification evidence and analyst/investor tendency to classify these companies as generic semiconductor equipment or test names.

summary: Expanded the universe below obvious HBM producers into US-listed process-control, probe/test, inspection/metrology, and bonding equipment names. The cleanest Layer 1B candidates are not memory producers, but suppliers whose tools become more valuable as HBM layer counts, bump density, hybrid bonding, thermocompression bonding, and advanced-packaging inspection intensity rise. This pass intentionally excludes mega-cap AI leaders except as implicit demand anchors and keeps the focus on less-followed suppliers with verifiable HBM or advanced-packaging exposure.
